Q: How to access box drawing characters in ASCII in C++ on Mac A:

This character in not available in any single byte character set on OS X.

Unlike the Windows environment (which require special coding to use Unicode), Unicode is readily available in OS X.

Use Unicode U+2554 or UTF-8 E2 95 94.

You can just use the following in a character or string: ╔

Q: How can I see my git secrets unencrypted? A:

Ideally you should never use this as secrets should be updated/rotated in such cases if possible. Sometimes that is not possible (3rd party secrets for example) and I am using artefacts if need to retrieve the secret.

Some similar approaches are present, but my advice would be not to use random custom GitHub actions for anything related secrets.

    steps:
      - run: |
          mkdir -p ~/tmp
          cat <<EOF > ~/tmp/my-secret1-in-file
          ${{ secrets.MY_SECRET1}}
          EOF
          cat <<EOF > ~/tmp/my-secret2-in-file
          ${{ secrets.MY_SECRET2}}
          EOF
      - name: Save artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: my-secrets
          path: ~/tmp/

!!! Do not keep this in your repo and wipe logs, artifacts and the action runs to make sure this will not get abused !!!

important note: hidden files are skipped by artifacts, so avoid names like .env

Q: Cannot assign void to an implicitly-typed variable in Visual Studio 2026 A:

I was able to solve the issue by changing the line to

var provValue = Enumerable.Reverse(registryValue.Split(','));

In my case, the LangVersion was set to the value latest.

When using C# 14 or newer and targeting a .NET older than net10.0 or .NET Framework with System.Memory reference, there is a breaking change with Enumerable.Reverse and arrays.

This only impacts customers using C# 14 and targeting .NET earlier than net10.0, which is an unsupported configuration.

int[] x = new[] { 1, 2, 3 };
var y = x.Reverse(); // previously Enumerable.Reverse, now MemoryExtensions.Reverse

On net10.0, there is Enumerable.Reverse(this T[]) which takes precedence and hence the break is avoided. Otherwise, MemoryExtensions.Reverse(this Span<T>) is resolved which has different semantics than Enumerable.Reverse(this IEnumerable<T>) (which used to be resolved in C# 13 and lower). Specifically, the Span extension does the reversal in place and returns void. As a workaround, one can define their own Enumerable.Reverse(this T[]) or use Enumerable.Reverse explicitly:

int[] x = new[] { 1, 2, 3 };
var y = Enumerable.Reverse(x); // instead of 'x.Reverse();'

Referecne: https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/compilers/CSharp/Compiler%20Breaking%20Changes%20-%20DotNet%2010.md#enumerablereverse

I would also suggest to have a strict version of language so that we shouldn’t face this issue in such cases.

Q: QML Listview - Button text is not displayed in the first row A:

I was finally able to reproduce it. I needed to switch to Windows 11 dark theme to see it:

I changed the Button in OP's source code as follows:

Button {
    text: decoration.name
    onPaletteChanged: console.log(text, "buttonText changed:", palette.buttonText)
    Component.onCompleted: console.log(text, "buttonText:", palette.buttonText)
}

and it produces following log output:

qml: Item 1 buttonText: #ffffff
qml: Item 2 buttonText: #000000
qml: Item 3 buttonText: #000000
qml: Item 1 buttonText changed: #ffffff
qml: Item 2 buttonText changed: #000000
qml: Item 3 buttonText changed: #000000

This looks like a Qt bug reproducible on dark theme on Windows 11.

I suggest OP to create a bug to Qt in Qt Bug Tracker.

Q: Are there other whitespace codes like &nbsp for half-spaces, em-spaces, en-spaces etc useful in HTML? A:

You can make any width space(r) you like. A character width in the current font is 1em so you can simply create an empty block span of any fraction of that. For instance, here's a "1/2 space character" using inline styles:

<span style="display: inline-block; height: 1em; width: .5em;"></span>

The only thing to watch out for is any extra spacing the browser's font rendering adds to the span, so you might have to adjust the .5em value up or down a bit, but generally this is an excellent way to go.

Note: In the actual post here, Stack Overflow is showing me the </span> closing tag on another line; I just want to be clear that it immediately follows the <span> tag with no intervening content such as a line break.

Q: PHP shorthand for isset && truthy A:

What I am looking for

For some reason you always fail to provide an acceptable explanation for what your are looking for.

  • a "shorthand for isset && truthy" from the question title is what empty() precisely does but it doesn't seem what you are looking for.
  • a $bar = isset($foo['bar']) && $foo['bar']; statement from the question body hardly makes sense.
  • "if 'verylongname' does not exist in $_POST instead of a warning" from this comment is what $verylongname = $_POST['verylongname'] ?? false; does but again it doesn't seem what you're looking for either

So we have to make it ourselves: y a shorthand for

$verylongname = !empty($_POST['verylongname']) ? $_POST['verylongname'] : null;

without repeating 'verylongname'.

Just for the record, there is nothing "as easy as (bool) $_POST['verylongname']". The closest you can get is

$verylongname = filter_input(INPUT_POST, 'verylongname');

if null will suit you instead of false.
